definition: A technique that caps the magnitude of gradients during training to prevent instability from exploding gradients.
details: Gradient clipping is especially important when training recurrent networks and large transformers, where occasional large gradients can otherwise destabilize optimization.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. In plain words: A technique that caps the magnitude of gradients during training to prevent instability from exploding gradients. Here is how it actually plays out: Gradient clipping is especially important when training recurrent networks and large transformers, where occasional large gradients can otherwise destabilize optimization. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Gradient Clipping.
